new_defects.title: /hi/destination/shimla SSR jumped from 1.68s to 5.16s in 24h (3x regression)
new_defects.evidence: curl TIME_TOTAL on /hi/destination/shimla today = 5.16s; yesterday 1.68s. /hi/destination/manali also 43% slower today (3.81s vs 2.67s yesterday). Both EN counterparts unchanged (Shimla EN: 2.44s today vs 2.46s yesterday; Manali EN: 2.87s today vs 2.04s). Pattern points to an HI locale regression on Himachal-Pradesh-state destinations (or a cold cache effect on infrequently hit HI pages — but two consecutive HI HP destinations is suspicious).
new_defects.impact: Slow Hindi destination pages disproportionately hurt the target persona (Hindi-speaking domestic traveler). Doubles back to BUG-005's i18n improvement work.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web destination route — investigate HI-locale render path for HP-state destinations; check for synchronous translation lookups or larger HI payloads.
new_defects.reproduction: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'hi_shimla=%{time_total}s en_shimla=' https://www.nakshiq.com/hi/destination/shimla; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}s\n' https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/shimla; done

new_defects.title: /api/weather is uncached — 3.29s for a single-city OpenWeatherMap proxy
new_defects.evidence: GET /api/weather?id=shimla returned 200 in 3.29s with payload {"temp":26,"feels_like":25,"humidity":18,"description":"overcast clouds",...,"updated":"2026-04-27T02:16:36.692Z"}. The 'updated' timestamp matches the request time — there is no edge cache or persistence layer between users and the upstream OpenWeatherMap call. /api/alerts?id=shimla returned in 1.10s with empty alerts (also looks uncached but cheaper).
new_defects.impact: Every destination page detail load triggers a fresh OWM round-trip. Adds 1–3s to the fetch waterfall on every destination page load and exposes the site to OWM rate limits / outages. Doubles user-perceived latency on flaky mobile (Ladakh 4G, R4 §5).
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web /api/weather route — add a 5–10 minute Vercel edge cache (s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=3600) keyed on destination id.
new_defects.reproduction: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'weather=%{time_total}s alerts=' 'https://www.nakshiq.com/api/weather?id=shimla'; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}s\n' 'https://www.nakshiq.com/api/alerts?id=shimla'; done

new_defects.impact: Internal linking gap: any user clicking 'Tamil Nadu' from a Karnataka neighbour or from a footer state list hits a hard 404. Compounds with the Kerala 404 which is still active today.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web region route — generate region landing pages from the supabase regions/destinations join, or hard-code missing states.

new_defects.title: Soft-404 catch-all confirmed beyond /destination — bad slugs return 200 + homepage HTML in BOTH locales
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200 in 1.25s with 73,683 bytes (matches the 73,595 byte EN homepage payload — soft-404). GET /hi/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200 in 1.38s with 84,349 bytes (matches the 84,313 byte HI homepage). Same defect family as yesterday's numeric-month soft-404 (NEW-2026-04-26-002) and confirms the destination [slug] handler returns the homepage instead of 404 when no record matches. Pattern is locale-symmetric.
new_defects.impact: Google sees thousands of duplicate-content soft-404 URLs and risks deranking. AI agents (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot) following llms.txt to numeric month URLs land on the homepage. Damages both organic SEO and AI-citability — both core moats per R1+R2.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web src/app/[locale]/destination/[id]/page.tsx — when supabase returns no row for the slug, call notFound() from next/navigation instead of falling through to homepage rendering.

new_defects.title: hreflang link tags STILL MISSING site-wide (carried from 2026-04-26 NEW-001 — no fix shipped)
new_defects.evidence: grep -c 'hreflang' on freshly fetched /en/destination/jaipur, /hi/destination/jaipur, /en home, /hi home, /en/destination/shimla, /hi/destination/munnar: ALL ZERO. og:locale present and correctly set to en_IN / hi_IN, but the link-rel=alternate hreflang pairs that signal translations to Google are absent.
new_defects.impact: Google can't pair /en/destination/jaipur with /hi/destination/jaipur as locale alternates. Hindi-search users may see EN page in SERPs (and vice versa). Direct hit on the R1 §3.2 i18n audit which was supposed to be ✓.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web/src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx — add <link rel='alternate' hreflang='en' href='...'/> + hreflang='hi' + hreflang='x-default' in the <head>. Should be derivable from next-intl's locale routing.

new_defects.impact: Mobile users on flaky connections (Ladakh 4G, R4 §5) face a 7s+ cold load. LCP on this page will fail Core Web Vitals. Carries forward as still-active.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web cost-index route — paginate or virtualize the cost rows, or split into city-by-city sub-pages.

The contract break persists.

new_defects.title: Leaflet map renders 0 markers on destination pages (now reproduced on 3 destinations)
new_defects.evidence: Live browser inspection — /en/destination/shimla (21 places claimed, 0 markers, 21 tiles loaded), /en/destination/manali (23 places claimed, 0 markers, 14 tiles loaded), /en/destination/jaipur (20 places claimed, 0 markers). All measured after 3.5s wait. .leaflet-container present, .leaflet-marker-pane present but empty in all three cases. Confirms BUG-007 is universal across destinations, not slug-specific.
new_defects.impact: User trust erosion: 'You said 20 places, I see 0 dots'. Undermines the data-confidence positioning. Disables 'find ATM / SOS pin / hospital' map affordances. Same defect family as BUG-007.
new_defects.recommended_owner: apps/web destination map component — likely a hydration/data-flow gap between server-rendered place list and client Leaflet init. Inspect props passed to map vs DOM order at hydration.

gaps: PerformanceObserver for LCP/FCP returned 0 buffered entries from chrome-extension execution context. Used DCL/loadEventEnd as proxies. Same gap as 2026-04-26 — not yet fixed.
